does: Works ground spices, with fresh garlic, ginger or chilli, salt and a little liquid, into a thick paste by pounding or blending. The paste clings to fish, meat or vegetables, and seasons them all over.

intro.what: This method works spices and fresh aromatics with just enough liquid to make a thick coating.
intro.why: It teaches you to join dry powders evenly while keeping the paste thick enough to cling to food.

how: Pound or blend the garlic, ginger and fresh chilli with the salt to a rough mash. The salt helps break them down.
Add a little liquid, such as water, lemon juice or yogurt, a spoonful at a time, and work it in.
Stop when the paste is thick and smooth, and holds on the spoon without running.
Use it at once, or let it stand briefly so the flavours join.

cues.text: The paste is an even deep colour with no dry streaks of powder.
It clings to the spoon and does not run off.

mistakes.mistake: Adding all the liquid at once, so that the paste runs off the food.
mistakes.fix: Add it a spoonful at a time and stop when the paste clings.

mistakes.mistake: Frying the raw paste on a high heat, so that the powders scorch.
mistakes.fix: Cook it gently, with a splash of liquid, or use it as a coating.

quiz.question: What consistency should a coating spice paste have?
choices: Thin enough to pour away from the food.
Dry powder that will not join the aromatics.
Thick enough to cling rather than run off.
quiz.because: The paste needs enough moisture to combine but enough body to stay on the food.

quiz.question: How should liquid enter the spice mixture?
choices: All at once before checking the thickness.
Keep adding after it already runs freely.
quiz.because: Gradual additions let you stop at a paste that clings instead of becoming too thin.

quiz.question: Which appearance suggests the powders are evenly mixed?
choices: Dry powder patches over a wet mash.
An even colour without dry streaks.
A clear liquid layer surrounding loose spices.
quiz.because: No dry streaks show the powders and aromatics have joined the paste.

quiz.question: Strong frying heat scorched the spice paste. What would you change next time?
choices: Continue frying dry until the powders darken.
Increase heat to drive off every trace of moisture quickly.
Cook it gently with a little liquid, or use it as a coating.
quiz.because: Gentler cooking and some liquid limit scorching of the ground spices.

comes_after.why: A paste starts with aromatics pounded and broken down with salt.
